```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
survey <- read_rds(here("data/processed/survey_clean.rds"))
canvassing <- read_rds(here("data/processed/canvassing_clean.rds"))
data_through <- max(as_date(survey$submitted_at), as_date(canvassing$submitted_at))
```

The Urban Institute is the research partner to
[Caring Across Generations](https://caringacross.org/) on the 1M Conversations
About Care initiative: families across the country sharing their experiences
with care through a digital survey, doorstep canvassing, and interviews. These
pages document how Urban handles that data and what it shows so far.

**Data through `r format(data_through, "%B %e, %Y")`**: `r format(nrow(survey), big.mark = ",")` survey
responses and `r nrow(canvassing)` canvassing contacts.

## What's here

[**Cleaning**](scripts/01_clean-data.qmd) — how the raw exports become
analysis files, step by step, with the checks that run on every delivery.
Read this to understand what each column in the data means and what we do
when a delivery looks different from the last one.

[**Chartbook**](scripts/survey/01_chartbook.qmd) — who is responding and what
they are saying: response counts by state and tool, urban and rural, survey
demographics, care pathways, challenges, supports, and what ideal care would
look like.

[**Variables**](variables.qmd) — a reference for every column in the clean
files: the question it came from and the answer text behind it.

[**Coding dashboard**](https://ui-research.github.io/one-million-care-conversations/)
— the interview transcripts coded against the project codebook, for review by
the qualitative team.

## Two things to keep in mind

- The three tools reach different people in different ways and are always
  reported separately.
- These are the people who chose to respond. Nothing here is nationally
  representative, and Urban never describes it that way.
